road:URB_ST.name: Urban Street / Residential Lane
road:URB_ST.summary: Interior colony / ward streets, residential by-lanes, service roads. Lower default speed (30 km/h is the recommended IRC residential limit). Pedestrians and children frequently on the carriageway.

speed_limits.notes: IRC:106 and IRC:103 recommend 30 km/h for residential streets. Many municipalities formally notify this.

key_rules.rule: Yielding to pedestrians at all crossings
Reverse driving / U-turn at intersections
Parking blocking residential gates / fire-tender access
Idling commercial vehicle (food delivery / cab waiting)
Modified silencers / noisy bikes ('bullet' patta)

what_to_check: Children playing
Stray animals
Cycle / e-rickshaw blind-spots

road:FOREST.name: Reserved / Protected Forest Road
road:FOREST.summary: Roads passing through Reserved Forests, Protected Forests, Wildlife Sanctuaries, National Parks or Tiger Reserves. Movement is regulated by the Indian Forest Act 1927, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972, and the State Forest Department's notifications.

speed_limits.notes: Frequently enforced via fixed cameras on NH-766 (Bandipur), NH-67 (Mudumalai), NH-44 (Pench).

key_rules.rule: Exceeding posted forest speed limit
key_rules.section: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 §27 + state forest dept order

key_rules.rule: Honking inside a sanctuary / national park
Stopping / alighting from the vehicle
Use of high-beam / spotlights at night where permitted
Carrying weapons / hunting equipment
Off-road driving (any deviation from the road)
Plastic / single-use carry-bags
key_rules.section: Plastic Waste Mgmt Rules 2016 + Forest Dept notification

what_to_check: Gate opening / closing time for the day
Carry no plastic, no firearms, no drone
Top-up fuel before entry — there's usually no fuel station inside

road:URB_ART.name: Urban Arterial / City Main Road
road:URB_ART.summary: City arterials — ring roads, trunk roads, flyovers, BRT corridors. Highest traffic-police enforcement density. Local Police Commissioner orders frequently override default rules (one-way, peak-hour bans).

speed_limits.notes: Frequently posted lower (40 km/h on flyovers, 30 km/h in dense markets).

key_rules.rule: Jumping a traffic signal
Lane indiscipline / weaving
Wrong parking (no-parking zone, on footpath, double-parking)
Triple riding on two-wheeler
Honking in silence zone (within 100 m of school/hospital/court)
Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate not produced
Bus-lane / BRT lane violation

what_to_check: PUC valid
Helmet/seat-belt
Avoid peak-hour HGV bans (most cities ban heavy vehicles 8–11 am and 5–10 pm)

road:PROHIB.name: Prohibited / No-Public-Access Area
road:PROHIB.summary: Areas formally NOTIFIED as 'prohibited places' under §2(8) of the Official Secrets Act, 1923 — atomic energy installations, ISRO/DRDO test ranges, missile silos, nuclear power plants, ammunition depots, and certain border outposts. Approaching, sketching or photographing any part of such a place — even from outside — can be prosecuted.

key_rules.rule: Entering or being in the vicinity of a prohibited place
key_rules.fine_inr: Imprisonment up to 14 years (espionage scale) or up to 3 years (general)

key_rules.rule: Photographing / video / drone surveillance of a prohibited place
Disobeying a lawful direction by a sentry
Carrying communication device into a 'no-electronics' bay

what_to_check: If you accidentally entered, STOP, switch off the engine, raise your hands, and follow sentry instructions exactly. Do NOT reach for your phone.

road:CANT.name: Army Cantonment Road
road:CANT.summary: Roads inside a Cantonment are governed by the Cantonments Act, 2006 and the Cantonment Board's traffic notifications. Civilian vehicles are usually permitted on through-roads but PHOTO-ID and vehicle inspection at the gate are common. Unauthorised entry is an offence under the Official Secrets Act, 1923 if the area is notified.

speed_limits.notes: Strictly enforced by Military Police (CMP) and Cantonment Board officers.

key_rules.rule: Photography / videography of military installations
key_rules.fine_inr: Imprisonment 3–14 years on conviction; on-the-spot device seizure

key_rules.rule: Unauthorised entry into a notified prohibited place
Speeding inside Cantonment

fine_inr.note: Cantt Board may impose additional cost-recovery

key_rules.rule: Parking on a Cantonment road without a permit
Carrying alcohol / tobacco into 'dry' sectors
Use of horn in any Cantonment area

what_to_check: Carry photo ID for every adult occupant
Vehicle RC + DL must match (rented vehicles carry a copy of the rental agreement)
Switch off dashcams when entering and follow sentry instructions

road:MDR.name: Major District Road (MDR)
road:MDR.summary: MDRs link talukas and major villages to the SH/NH network. Maintained by State PWD or Zilla Parishad. Mixed traffic (cars, trucks, two-wheelers, tractors, animal-drawn) is the norm.

key_rules.rule: MV Act applies in full
Mandatory horn use is restricted in silence zones near schools/hospitals
Overloading of goods carriages
Carrying excess passengers on motorcycle (>1 pillion)

what_to_check: RC + DL + insurance current
Avoid night travel — many MDRs lack lighting
Check for unmanned level crossings

road:PRIVATE.name: Private / Gated Community / Campus Road
road:PRIVATE.summary: Roads inside an apartment society, gated layout, factory, university campus, or industrial estate. Even though the road is private, it qualifies as a 'public place' under §2(34) of the MV Act if the public has access — therefore the MV Act applies.

speed_limits.notes: RWA / management can post even lower; abide by signage.

key_rules.rule: MV Act §185 (drunk driving), §184 (rash driving), §128 (pillion safety) apply on private roads with public access
RWA byelaws on visitor passes / parking sticker
Gate-jumping / damage to boom-barrier
key_rules.fine_inr: Up to 6 months imprisonment + repair cost

key_rules.rule: CCTV-based wrong-side / wrong-parking enforcement

what_to_check: Visitor entry register / app
Gate timing
Speed-bumps placement

road:SCHOOL_ZONE.name: School / Hospital / Silence Zone
road:SCHOOL_ZONE.summary: 100 m buffer around schools, hospitals, courts and religious places is a 'silence zone' under the Noise Pollution Rules. Many cities also enforce 25 km/h speed limit and ban honking entirely.

speed_limits.notes: Posted on yellow signage. Violations are non-compoundable in some states.

key_rules.rule: Honking in a silence zone
key_rules.section: Noise Pollution (Reg & Control) Rules 2000 r/w EPA 1986

key_rules.rule: Over-speeding in school zone
Mobile phone while driving (zero-tolerance in zone)
Drop-off/pick-up only in marked zones; no double-row halting

what_to_check: School-hour windows (typically 7:30–9:30 and 1:30–4:30)
Marshal direction overrides signal phase

road:ODR.name: Other District / Rural / Village Road (ODR / VR / PMGSY)
road:ODR.summary: Village-level roads — often single-lane, mixed-traffic, frequently maintained under PMGSY (Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana). MV Act applies on every public way regardless of surface.

speed_limits.notes: Often unposted; assume 50 km/h max and reduce in habitations.

key_rules.rule: MV Act applies even on unpaved village roads if they are 'public places'
Animal-drawn vehicles must carry reflective tape after dusk
Riding on the wrong side / against the flow
Overloading of passengers in goods carriers (common practice but illegal)

what_to_check: Daylight travel preferred
Spare tyre + basic tools
Carry water/fuel for long stretches

road:SH.name: State Highway
road:SH.summary: State Highways connect district HQs and major towns within a state and are maintained by the State PWD. The MV Act applies; states may publish their own compounding tables under Section 200 and Section 210A.

speed_limits.notes: Reduced to 50 km/h within municipal limits unless otherwise posted.

key_rules.rule: All Central MV Act provisions apply
Overtaking only on the right; no overtaking at curves / level crossings
State-specific over-speed multiplier (where notified)
key_rules.fine_inr: Up to 0.5x – 1.0x of the central rate. Check the matched state pack.

key_rules.rule: Bull-ock carts / agricultural tractors permitted but must use shoulder where available
Pillion safety on two-wheelers (helmet)

what_to_check: RC + DL + insurance + PUC current
Posted speed at municipal-limit boards
Whether the state has notified additional fine multipliers

road:EXP.name: Expressway / Access-Controlled Highway
road:EXP.summary: Expressways are access-controlled, divided carriageways with grade-separated entry/exit. Two-wheelers, three-wheelers, tractors and non-motorised traffic are typically PROHIBITED. Maximum legal speed is 120 km/h for cars (CMVR amendment, 2018).

speed_limits.notes: Posted limit prevails. Some expressways (Yamuna, Samruddhi) enforce 100 km/h via section-speed cameras.

key_rules.rule: Two-wheelers, three-wheelers, tractors, bullock carts and pedestrians are prohibited
key_rules.section: Section 5 of Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002 + state expressway notifications

key_rules.rule: Mandatory minimum speed in fast lane
Stopping on shoulder except for genuine emergency
Wrong-side driving
Section-speed enforcement (average speed cameras)

fine_inr.note: Photographic challan; payable online via VAHAN.

key_rules.rule: FASTag mandatory at all toll plazas
U-turn / reversing on the carriageway

what_to_check: Vehicle is allowed on this expressway (check signage at on-ramp)
Fuel for full segment — many expressways have 60–80 km between fuel stations
FASTag balance

road:PORT.name: Major Port / Port-Trust Area
road:PORT.summary: Internal roads of a Major Port (JNPT, Mumbai, Chennai, Mundra, Kandla, Kolkata, Visakhapatnam, etc.) or a State Maritime Board jetty are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act 2021 (or state Act) and the Port Trust's traffic byelaws.

speed_limits.notes: Lower in liquid-cargo and cryogenic zones.

key_rules.rule: Entry without an active e-Gate-Pass / FASTag terminal token
Unauthorised entry into a customs-bond area
Carrying restricted goods / liquor / weapons inside the port
key_rules.section: Customs Act + Arms Act + state excise

key_rules.rule: Photographing the port, ships, or CISF posts
Speeding inside a marine-loading bay
Flammable cargo without 'Hazmat' placard

what_to_check: e-Gate pass valid for the day & gate
Driver licence + vehicle RC inspection at gate
Hi-vis vest + safety shoes for any walking inside the yard

road:TOLL_PLAZA.name: Toll Plaza / Approach
road:TOLL_PLAZA.summary: 200-metre approach to a toll plaza on NH/Expressway. Strict 25 km/h limit and lane-discipline rules apply. FASTag is mandatory in all four-wheelers (Notification S.O. 5249(E), 24-Dec-2019).

key_rules.rule: No FASTag in a FASTag-only lane
key_rules.fine_inr: Double the toll for the segment

key_rules.rule: Wait time > 10 seconds permits free passage (Industry SOP)
Reverse driving / U-turn at the plaza
Lane-cutting near the plaza
Refusal to pay without genuine grievance

what_to_check: FASTag balance ≥ expected toll
Vehicle category matches FASTag class
Toll receipt (digital) — required for re-entry within 24 h same direction

road:NH.name: National Highway
road:NH.summary: National Highways are owned by the Centre (MoRTH) and built/maintained by NHAI or state PWDs. The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019) and CMVR 1989 apply with national speed schedules and tolling under the National Highways Act, 1956.

speed_limits.notes: Maximum speed (Notification GSR 359(E), 6-Apr-2018). Local NH segments through built-up areas may post lower limits — the posted sign always prevails.

key_rules.rule: Lane discipline (right-most for overtaking only)
Helmet mandatory for both rider and pillion
Seat belt mandatory for ALL occupants (front + rear)
Driving without valid licence
Drunk driving (BAC > 30 mg / 100 ml blood)
Mobile phone while driving
Over-speeding > 20 km/h above limit
Stopping / parking on the carriageway except in emergencies
FASTag required for all four-wheelers (Section 8(b) of National Highways Fee Rules 2008)
key_rules.fine_inr: Double the toll for non-FASTag in dedicated lanes

what_to_check: Valid DL + RC + Insurance + PUC
FASTag balance (avoid 2x toll penalty)
Reflective triangle and first-aid kit (recommended; mandatory for HGV)

road:BORDER.name: Border Road (BRO)
road:BORDER.summary: Roads built and maintained by the Border Roads Organisation under the Ministry of Defence. Many are dual-use (civilian + military). Inner Line Permit (ILP) or Protected Area Permit (PAP) is required for most non-residents to travel beyond a notified line.

speed_limits.notes: Posted ‘BRO speed governor’ signs every 5 km. Convoy timings (one-way windows) are common at Rohtang, Zoji La, Sela, Khardung La.

key_rules.rule: Travel without ILP / PAP where required
key_rules.section: Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation 1873 + Foreigners (Protected Areas) Order 1958

fine_inr.first: Detention + deportation for foreigners; prosecution for Indians

key_rules.rule: Photography of bunkers / pickets / ICPs / radar
Convoy timing violation (entering a one-way window in the wrong direction)

fine_inr.first: Vehicle held until reverse window opens; ₹1000+

key_rules.rule: Drone / GPS-tracker beyond inner line
Carrying banned items (foreign sat-phones, narcotics, satellite imagery)

what_to_check: Permit validity, route, dates
Convoy / one-way schedule for the day
Carry water, oxygen-can, warm gear in winter
Inform local check-post on entry & exit

road:DEF.name: Defence Establishment / Military Operational Area
road:DEF.summary: Areas under the operational control of the Indian Army, Navy, Air Force, BSF, ITBP, SSB, CRPF, CISF, Coast Guard, or DRDO/ISRO testing ranges. Public access is by EXPLICIT WRITTEN PERMIT only. Photographing or sketching the establishment is an offence under the Official Secrets Act, 1923.

speed_limits.notes: Internal traffic only; civilians normally not present.

key_rules.rule: Photography / videography / sketching of any establishment
Unauthorised entry / loitering near perimeter
key_rules.section: Official Secrets Act, 1923 §3 + Indian Penal Code §188

key_rules.rule: Operating UAV / drone within 5 km of an airbase
key_rules.section: Aircraft Rules 1937 r/w UAS Rules 2021 + Aircraft (Amendment) Act 2020
key_rules.fine_inr: Up to ₹1 lakh + drone confiscation; under DGCA criminal procedure

key_rules.rule: Carrying GPS jammers / radio equipment without licence
Smoking / open flame near fuel or ammo dumps

what_to_check: Confirm pass validity (date, gate, vehicle number)
Phone, dashcam, drone, and camera will be sealed at the gate
Inform sentry of any electronic device on you

vio:HWY_LANE_INDICATOR.name: Failure to use turn-indicator on expressway
vio:HWY_LANE_INDICATOR.description: Merging / overtaking without turn indicator on expressway.
keywords: failure to use turn-indicator on expressway

vio:HWY_STOP_ON_SHOULDER.name: Stopping on highway shoulder / express lane
vio:HWY_STOP_ON_SHOULDER.what_to_do_next: Move on at once unless breakdown — then switch hazard lights + reflective triangle 15m behind.
vio:HWY_STOP_ON_SHOULDER.tips_to_avoid: Keep emergency kit: triangle, torch, jack, spare tube/tyre.
keywords: stopping on highway shoulder / express lane

vio:HWY_MIN_SPEED_VIOLATION.name: Driving below minimum prescribed speed (expressway)
vio:HWY_MIN_SPEED_VIOLATION.what_to_do_next: Speed up to prescribed minimum (usually 60 kph) or exit expressway.

vio:HWY_REVERSING_HIGHWAY.name: Reversing on highway / expressway
vio:HWY_REVERSING_HIGHWAY.what_to_do_next: Extremely dangerous. Drive to next U-turn / exit.

vio:HWY_TRUCK_LEFT_LANE.name: Truck not using leftmost lane on expressway
keywords: truck not using leftmost lane on expressway

vio:OVERLOAD_ROOFTOP_LUGGAGE.name: Unsecured rooftop / extra luggage beyond limits
keywords: unsecured rooftop / extra luggage beyond limits

vio:OVERLOAD_GOODS_WEIGHT.name: Overloading a goods vehicle by weight
vio:OVERLOAD_GOODS_WEIGHT.what_to_do_next: Off-load excess at nearest weigh station. Pay ₹20,000 + ₹2,000 per extra tonne.
keywords: overloading a goods vehicle by weight

vio:OVERLOAD_PASSENGER.name: Overloading of passenger vehicle
vio:OVERLOAD_PASSENGER.what_to_do_next: Drop extra passengers; ₹200 per extra passenger.

vio:PARK_DISABLED_SPOT.name: Parking in disabled-reserved spot without permit
vio:PARK_DISABLED_SPOT.what_to_do_next: Vacate immediately. Only disabled-permit holders may park.
keywords: parking in disabled-reserved spot without permit

vio:PARK_FIRE_HYDRANT.name: Parking blocking fire hydrant / emergency access
vio:PARK_FIRE_HYDRANT.what_to_do_next: Move at once. Fine ₹500–1,000; vehicle may be forcibly removed in emergency.
keywords: parking blocking fire hydrant / emergency access

vio:PARK_ABANDONED.name: Abandoned vehicle on road
vio:PARK_ABANDONED.what_to_do_next: Claim vehicle at nearest police station within 30 days or it will be auctioned.

vio:PARK_NO_PARKING.name: Parking in no-parking zone
vio:PARK_NO_PARKING.what_to_do_next: Move vehicle immediately; pay ₹500 first-time, ₹1,000 repeat + towing ₹500–1,500.
vio:PARK_NO_PARKING.irc_sign_ref: IRC 67 — Sign No. R-14 'No Parking' (blue circle red cross).
vio:PARK_NO_PARKING.officer_action: Photo challan or towing crane lifts vehicle to impound lot.

vio:PARK_NIGHT_NO_LIGHTS.name: Parked vehicle without parking lights at night
keywords: parked vehicle without parking lights at night

vio:PARK_FOOTPATH.name: Parking on footpath / pedestrian area
vio:PARK_FOOTPATH.what_to_do_next: Pedestrians have absolute right of way. Pay ₹500–1,000.

vio:PARK_BUS_STOP.name: Parking at bus stop / taxi stand
keywords: parking at bus stop / taxi stand

vio:PARK_DOUBLE_PARKING.name: Double parking / parking away from kerb
vio:PARK_DOUBLE_PARKING.description: Leaving a vehicle that causes obstruction.
vio:PARK_DOUBLE_PARKING.what_to_do_next: Park parallel to kerb within 30 cm. Move now.
keywords: double parking / parking away from kerb

vio:PARK_EV_SPOT_MISUSE.name: Non-EV parked in EV-reserved charging spot
vio:PARK_EV_SPOT_MISUSE.description: ICE vehicle occupying an EV-marked parking + charging bay. Primarily municipal-level penalty.
keywords: non-ev parked in ev-reserved charging spot

vio:EV_UNREG_RETROFIT.name: Unauthorised ICE→EV retrofit without RTO approval
vio:EV_UNREG_RETROFIT.what_to_do_next: Stop plying. Retrofit kit must be ARAI / ICAT certified; RTO re-registration mandatory.
keywords: unauthorised ice→ev retrofit without rto approval

vio:EV_FIRE_BATTERY_NONCOMPLIANT.name: Use of non-AIS-156 compliant EV battery
keywords: use of non-ais-156 compliant ev battery

vio:EV_CHARGING_UNAUTH.name: Charging EV at unauthorised / domestic outlet in public place
vio:EV_CHARGING_UNAUTH.description: Using a non-approved public socket or commercial electricity tap for EV charging on street / pavement.
vio:EV_CHARGING_UNAUTH.what_to_do_next: Charge only at authorised public stations (Bharat EV / BECIL network).
vio:EV_CHARGING_UNAUTH.tips_to_avoid: App-find chargers — PlugShare, Tata Power EZ Charge, Ather Grid.
keywords: charging ev at unauthorised / domestic outlet in public place

vio:EV_RESTRICTED_ZONE_VIOLATION.name: Low-speed EV in restricted zone (e.g., highway)
keywords: low-speed ev in restricted zone (e.g., highway)

vio:DIR_WRONG_WAY.name: Driving on wrong side / opposite lane
vio:DIR_WRONG_WAY.description: Driving against the flow of traffic on a one-way or divided road.
vio:DIR_WRONG_WAY.what_to_do_next: Stop, turn around safely at next opening. Pay ₹1,500 first-time, ₹5,000 repeat.
vio:DIR_WRONG_WAY.tips_to_avoid: Follow divider colour: yellow on your right = correct side.
vio:DIR_WRONG_WAY.officer_action: ANPR / on-spot challan; higher fine in metros (Delhi, Mumbai — ₹5,000).
keywords: driving on wrong side / opposite lane

vio:DIR_FAIL_TO_YIELD.name: Failure to yield right of way
keywords: failure to yield right of way

vio:DIR_ILLEGAL_OVERTAKING.name: Overtaking from wrong side / in no-overtaking zone
vio:DIR_ILLEGAL_OVERTAKING.description: Overtaking on the left, on curves/bridges, or in no-overtaking zones.
vio:DIR_ILLEGAL_OVERTAKING.tips_to_avoid: Overtake only on right side of slower vehicle; never on bridges, curves, or near oncoming traffic.
keywords: overtaking from wrong side / in no-overtaking zone

vio:DIR_LANE_DISCIPLINE.name: Lane indiscipline / failing to keep to prescribed lane
vio:DIR_LANE_DISCIPLINE.description: Not keeping to designated lane (e.g., truck lane, BRTS lane).
vio:DIR_LANE_DISCIPLINE.what_to_do_next: Stay in assigned lane; use indicator before changing.
vio:DIR_LANE_DISCIPLINE.irc_sign_ref: IRC 67 — Sign No. M-4 'Keep Left' / 'Keep Right'.
keywords: lane indiscipline / failing to keep to prescribed lane

vio:DIR_BUS_TAXI_LANE.name: Using dedicated bus/taxi lane in violation
keywords: using dedicated bus/taxi lane in violation

vio:DIR_NO_ENTRY.name: Entering a no-entry zone
vio:DIR_NO_ENTRY.description: Entering area marked NO ENTRY (e.g., by time of day).
vio:DIR_NO_ENTRY.what_to_do_next: Back out or find approved detour; pay ₹500–1,000.
vio:DIR_NO_ENTRY.irc_sign_ref: IRC 67 — Sign No. 8 'No Entry' (red circle with white horizontal bar).

vio:DIR_NO_UTURN.name: Taking a U-turn where prohibited
vio:DIR_NO_UTURN.description: U-turn at a location marked NO U-TURN.
vio:DIR_NO_UTURN.what_to_do_next: Take the next approved U-turn; pay ₹500–1,000.

vio:DIR_ONE_WAY_VIOLATION.name: Entering one-way road from wrong direction
vio:DIR_ONE_WAY_VIOLATION.irc_sign_ref: IRC 67 — Sign No. 4 'One Way' (blue rectangle, white arrow).
keywords: entering one-way road from wrong direction
wrong way on a one way

vio:SAFETY_NO_HELMET_PILLION.name: Pillion rider not wearing helmet
vio:SAFETY_NO_HELMET_PILLION.what_to_do_next: Pillion must wear an ISI helmet; fine ₹1,000.
vio:SAFETY_NO_HELMET_PILLION.licence_action: Rider's licence may be disqualified for 3 months (s.194D)

vio:SAFETY_NO_CHILD_RESTRAINT.name: Child under 14 without helmet / child-restraint
vio:SAFETY_NO_CHILD_RESTRAINT.what_to_do_next: Install ISOFIX / age-appropriate child seat (CMVR 138A since 2023). Fine ₹1,000.
vio:SAFETY_NO_CHILD_RESTRAINT.tips_to_avoid: 0–1 yr: rear-facing; 1–4 yrs: forward-facing; 4–12 yrs: booster + belt.

vio:SAFETY_NO_CHILD_2W.name: Carrying child below 4 on 2W without safety harness + helmet
vio:SAFETY_NO_CHILD_2W.description: Children below 4 must be secured with a safety harness and must wear a crash helmet; 2W speed capped at 40 km/h when carrying such a child.
vio:SAFETY_NO_CHILD_2W.what_to_do_next: Child < 4 yrs: must wear crash helmet + be tethered with safety harness. Max speed 40 kph.
keywords: carrying child below 4 on 2w without safety harness + helmet

vio:SAFETY_NO_SEATBELT_PASSENGER.name: Passenger (incl. rear) not wearing seat belt
vio:SAFETY_NO_SEATBELT_PASSENGER.what_to_do_next: All passengers including rear must wear seat belts (post-2022 enforcement). Pay ₹1,000 per passenger.
keywords: passenger (incl. rear) not wearing seat belt
seat belt in the back seat

vio:SAFETY_NO_HELMET_RIDER.name: Rider not wearing helmet
vio:SAFETY_NO_HELMET_RIDER.what_to_do_next: Put on an ISI-marked helmet (IS 4151). Pay ₹1,000; DL may be suspended 3 months.
vio:SAFETY_NO_HELMET_RIDER.tips_to_avoid: Helmet must be buckled; 'half helmets' / construction helmets are NOT legal.
vio:SAFETY_NO_HELMET_RIDER.common_misconception: Pillion rider also needs a helmet — not just the main rider.

vio:SAFETY_NO_ADAS.name: Disabling / removing mandated ADAS features
vio:SAFETY_NO_ADAS.description: Removing or disabling mandated ADAS in vehicles where it is phased-in mandatory (phased rollout 2025-27).

vio:SAFETY_NO_AIRBAG.name: Selling / operating new LMV without dual front airbags
vio:SAFETY_NO_AIRBAG.description: Post-Oct 2022 MoRTH notification — dual front airbags mandatory in all new LMVs (M1 category).
keywords: selling / operating new lmv without dual front airbags

vio:SAFETY_NO_SEATBELT_DRIVER.name: Driver not wearing seat belt
vio:SAFETY_NO_SEATBELT_DRIVER.tips_to_avoid: Seat belts save ~45% of lives in front-seat crashes (WHO).

vio:SAFETY_MORE_THAN_2_ON_2W.name: More than 2 persons on a two-wheeler (triple riding)
vio:SAFETY_MORE_THAN_2_ON_2W.what_to_do_next: Drop the extra rider. Only 2 permitted. Fine ₹1,000.
keywords: more than 2 persons on a two-wheeler (triple riding)

vio:PED_ZEBRA_VIOLATION.name: Not giving way to pedestrian at zebra crossing
keywords: not giving way to pedestrian at zebra crossing

vio:PARK_ZEBRA_CROSSING.name: Stopping on zebra crossing / pedestrian crossing
keywords: stopping on zebra crossing / pedestrian crossing

vio:CYCLIST_DOORING.name: Opening door unsafely into cyclist / vehicle path
keywords: opening door unsafely into cyclist / vehicle path

vio:DIST_HEADPHONES.name: Driving while wearing headphones / both ears covered
vio:DIST_HEADPHONES.what_to_do_next: Remove headphones; single-ear Bluetooth okay in some states.
keywords: driving while wearing headphones / both ears covered

vio:DIST_MOBILE_USE.name: Using mobile phone while driving
vio:DIST_MOBILE_USE.description: Handheld mobile phone use. Hands-free navigation permitted.
vio:DIST_MOBILE_USE.what_to_do_next: Pull over safely to use phone. Pay ₹5,000 (1st) / ₹10,000 (repeat).
vio:DIST_MOBILE_USE.tips_to_avoid: Hands-free / voice navigation permitted. Use dashboard mount + Bluetooth.
vio:DIST_MOBILE_USE.common_misconception: Even at a red signal, phone use counts as the vehicle is still 'in use'.

vio:DOC_DRIVING_MENTALLY_UNFIT.name: Driving while mentally/physically unfit
vio:DOC_DRIVING_MENTALLY_UNFIT.description: Driving in a state of unfit health (e.g., poor vision, sedation).

vio:IMPAIRED_DRUGS.name: Driving under influence of drugs
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUGS.consequence: Same as drunk driving + possible NDPS proceedings.
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUGS.licence_action: Licence impounded and suspended (s.206(4) r/w s.19)

vio:IMPAIRED_REFUSE_TEST.name: Refusing breath / blood test
vio:IMPAIRED_REFUSE_TEST.what_to_do_next: Refusal itself is an offence — presumption of guilt.

vio:IMPAIRED_DRUNK.name: Drunk driving (BAC > 30 mg/100 ml blood)
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUNK.description: Alcohol in blood exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml or influence such that driving is impaired.
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUNK.what_to_do_next: Cooperate with breathalyser. Do not drive. Call a cab / sober friend.
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUNK.tips_to_avoid: Permissible BAC 30 mg/100 ml (~half pint of beer for most adults). Zero BAC required for commercial drivers in many states.
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUNK.officer_action: Breathalyser + FIR; DL suspended 6 months; imprisonment 6 months (1st), 2 yrs (repeat).
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUNK.consequence: Fine ₹10,000 + 6 months jail (1st); ₹15,000 + 2 yrs jail (repeat within 3 yrs).
vio:IMPAIRED_DRUNK.licence_action: Licence impounded and suspended (s.206(4) r/w s.19)

vio:FASTAG_TAMPERED.name: Use of tampered / duplicate FASTag
vio:FASTAG_TAMPERED.description: Tampered, duplicate or unlinked FASTag. ₹5,000–10,000 per instance (NHAI 2025 rules).
vio:FASTAG_TAMPERED.what_to_do_next: Blacklist reported; fine ₹5,000–10,000. Re-apply with correct KYC.

vio:COMM_AGGREGATOR_NO_LICENCE.name: Aggregator operating without state licence
vio:COMM_AGGREGATOR_NO_LICENCE.description: Ola / Uber / Rapido etc. operating in a state without aggregator licence. ₹25,000–1,00,000 per case + suspension.
vio:COMM_AGGREGATOR_NO_LICENCE.what_to_do_next: Aggregator must apply for licence under MV Aggregator Rules 2020. ₹25k–₹1L fine per case.

vio:COMM_SCHOOL_BUS_VIOLATION.name: School bus safety norms violation
vio:COMM_SCHOOL_BUS_VIOLATION.description: Missing CCTV/GPS, attendant, speed governor, yellow colour, first-aid.

vio:FASTAG_MULTI_VEHICLE.name: Same FASTag used across multiple vehicles
vio:FASTAG_MULTI_VEHICLE.description: One FASTag transferred between vehicles — blacklisting + fine.
keywords: same fastag used across multiple vehicles

vio:SCHOOL_BUS_GPS_CAMERA.name: School bus lacking CCTV + GPS + lady attendant
vio:SCHOOL_BUS_GPS_CAMERA.description: Post-2016 SC directions on school bus safety — CCTV inside bus, GPS / VLT, lady attendant, distinct yellow livery, speed governor.
vio:SCHOOL_BUS_GPS_CAMERA.what_to_do_next: Immediately comply: install VLT/GPS, CCTV, yellow livery, female attendant.
keywords: school bus lacking cctv + gps + lady attendant

vio:COMM_NO_GPS_VLTS.name: Commercial vehicle without GPS / VLTS (where mandated)
keywords: commercial vehicle without gps / vlts (where mandated)

vio:COMM_NO_FARE_METER.name: Taxi / auto without calibrated fare meter
vio:COMM_NO_FARE_METER.what_to_do_next: Install calibrated meter; get it re-stamped at Legal Metrology.
keywords: taxi / auto without calibrated fare meter

vio:COMM_REFUSAL.name: Refusal of hire by auto / taxi
vio:COMM_REFUSAL.what_to_do_next: Record complaint at https://transport.<state>.gov.in. Fine up to ₹500.
keywords: refusal of hire by auto / taxi

vio:COMM_RIDE_HAILING_REFUSAL.name: App-based cab / auto refusing fare
vio:COMM_RIDE_HAILING_REFUSAL.description: Refusal by a licensed aggregator driver — fine + possible de-platforming.

vio:COMM_OVERCHARGE.name: Overcharging by auto / taxi
keywords: asked for more money than the meter

vio:TOLL_EVASION.name: Toll evasion (breaking barrier / forced lane change)
vio:TOLL_EVASION.description: Evading payment at toll plaza. ₹5,000 + penalty of toll arrears.
vio:TOLL_EVASION.what_to_do_next: Pay toll + ₹5,000 penalty; repeat — FIR under BNS for criminal breach.
keywords: toll evasion (breaking barrier / forced lane change)

vio:FASTAG_NONE.name: No FASTag on National Highway toll plaza
vio:FASTAG_NONE.description: Entering a FASTag-only lane or toll plaza without a working FASTag. Double the standard user fee charged (NHAI 2021 rule).
vio:FASTAG_NONE.what_to_do_next: Pay 2x user fee at toll; buy FASTag at on-site counter or online (Paytm / HDFC / SBI).
vio:FASTAG_NONE.tips_to_avoid: FASTag is mandatory since 15-Feb-2021 on all NH / SH toll plazas.
keywords: no fastag on national highway toll plaza

vio:COMM_NO_PERMIT.name: Plying commercial vehicle without permit
vio:COMM_NO_PERMIT.what_to_do_next: Park vehicle. Apply for permit at RTO; ₹10,000 fine.

vio:ACC_CAUSING_DEATH.name: Causing death by negligent driving
vio:ACC_CAUSING_DEATH.what_to_do_next: Cooperate; legal counsel; victim's family entitled to ₹2L solatium (Sec 161).
vio:ACC_CAUSING_DEATH.consequence: BNS Sec 106 — up to 5 yrs jail + fine.

vio:EMERG_NO_WAY_TO_AMBULANCE.name: Not making way for emergency vehicle (ambulance / fire)
keywords: not making way for emergency vehicle (ambulance / fire)
didn't give way to an ambulance

vio:ACC_NOT_REPORT.name: Not reporting accident within 24 hours
vio:ACC_NOT_REPORT.what_to_do_next: Report at nearest PS within 24 hrs; collect DAR.

vio:ACC_HIT_AND_RUN_RELATED.name: Hit-and-run related offence (absconding)
vio:ACC_HIT_AND_RUN_RELATED.description: Person in charge absconding after accident; compounding fee.

vio:ACC_HIT_AND_RUN.name: Leaving the scene of an accident (hit-and-run)
vio:ACC_HIT_AND_RUN.what_to_do_next: Non-compoundable. Report to police within 24 hours under Sec 134.
vio:ACC_HIT_AND_RUN.tips_to_avoid: Stop, call 112, help injured (Good Samaritan Law protects helpers from harassment).
vio:ACC_HIT_AND_RUN.consequence: BNS Sec 106(2): up to 10 yrs jail for fatal hit-and-run (effective July 2024).
keywords: leaving the scene of an accident (hit-and-run)

vio:ACC_DRIVER_FATIGUE.name: Commercial driver exceeding driving-hour limit
vio:ACC_DRIVER_FATIGUE.description: Continuous driving >8 hours / >48 hours a week for commercial drivers is prohibited.

vio:DOC_UNDERAGE.name: Underage driving
vio:DOC_UNDERAGE.description: Driving by a person below the prescribed minimum age. Guardian held liable under Sec 199A.
vio:DOC_UNDERAGE.what_to_do_next: The juvenile must stop immediately. Guardian will receive summons. Vehicle registration will be cancelled for 12 months.
vio:DOC_UNDERAGE.tips_to_avoid: Minimum ages: 16 yrs (gearless ≤50cc), 18 yrs (geared motorcycle & LMV), 20 yrs (transport).
vio:DOC_UNDERAGE.officer_action: Vehicle seized; summons to guardian under Sec 199A.
vio:DOC_UNDERAGE.common_misconception: Letting a minor 'learn' on a vacant road is still an offence if the vehicle is on a public place.
vio:DOC_UNDERAGE.licence_action: Vehicle registration cancelled for 12 months; the juvenile cannot get a licence until 25 (s.199A)

vio:JUV_MINOR_DRIVING.name: Minor driving – guardian liability
vio:JUV_MINOR_DRIVING.description: Guardian & owner deemed guilty unless proven knowledge-absent.
vio:JUV_MINOR_DRIVING.licence_action: Vehicle registration cancelled for 12 months; the juvenile cannot get a licence until 25 (s.199A)

vio:SPEED_OVER_MMV_HMV.name: Over-speeding (medium/heavy vehicle)
vio:SPEED_OVER_MMV_HMV.tips_to_avoid: HMV national default 80 kph (NH), 60 kph (state roads); check speed governor.
vio:SPEED_OVER_MMV_HMV.officer_action: Speed camera challan; repeat can lead to DL suspension (3 months).
vio:SPEED_OVER_MMV_HMV.licence_action: Licence may be impounded on repeat (s.206(4))

vio:SPEED_EXCESSIVE_50PLUS.name: Exceeding speed limit by more than 50%
vio:SPEED_EXCESSIVE_50PLUS.description: Very high over-speeding is an aggravated offence.
vio:SPEED_EXCESSIVE_50PLUS.what_to_do_next: Cooperate — this is an aggravated offence with probable DL suspension.
vio:SPEED_EXCESSIVE_50PLUS.officer_action: Challan + DL suspension recommendation to RTO.
keywords: exceeding speed limit by more than 50%

vio:SPEED_IN_RESIDENTIAL_SCHOOL_ZONE.name: Speeding in school / residential / silence zone
vio:SPEED_IN_RESIDENTIAL_SCHOOL_ZONE.description: Exceeding posted slower limit in school/residential/hospital zones.
vio:SPEED_IN_RESIDENTIAL_SCHOOL_ZONE.what_to_do_next: Reduce to 25–30 kph in school zones. Pay compounded fine.
vio:SPEED_IN_RESIDENTIAL_SCHOOL_ZONE.tips_to_avoid: Keep school-hour awareness (07:30–09:30, 13:00–16:00); enforce limit even when no children visible.
vio:SPEED_IN_RESIDENTIAL_SCHOOL_ZONE.irc_sign_ref: IRC 67:2022 — Sign No. C-11 'School Ahead' (warning) + Sign No. 24 'Speed Limit 25'.
keywords: speeding in school / residential / silence zone

vio:SPEED_OVER_LMV.name: Over-speeding (LMV / car / 2W / 3W)
vio:SPEED_OVER_LMV.description: Exceeding the prescribed speed limit in an LMV category vehicle.
vio:SPEED_OVER_LMV.what_to_do_next: Slow down to posted limit. Pay ₹1,000–2,000 via e-challan.
vio:SPEED_OVER_LMV.tips_to_avoid: Use cruise control; follow posted signs; city default 50 kph unless signed otherwise.
vio:SPEED_OVER_LMV.irc_sign_ref: IRC 67:2022 — Sign No. 24 (Maximum Speed Limit, white circle red border).
vio:SPEED_OVER_LMV.evidence_req: Time-stamped photo with vehicle, speed, location.
vio:SPEED_OVER_LMV.licence_action: Licence may be impounded on repeat (s.206(4))

vio:MOD_FAKE_NUMBER_PLATE.name: Use of fake / copied number plate
vio:MOD_FAKE_NUMBER_PLATE.description: Mounted fake / cloned number plate; also a cognizable offence under criminal law.
keywords: use of fake / copied number plate

vio:MOD_FANCY_NUMBERPLATE.name: Stylised / fancy / illegible number plate font
vio:MOD_FANCY_NUMBERPLATE.what_to_do_next: Replace with standard HSRP in Charlie block font.
keywords: stylised / fancy / illegible number plate font

vio:SPEED_GOVERNOR_TAMPER.name: Tampering / disabling speed governor on commercial vehicle
vio:SPEED_GOVERNOR_TAMPER.description: Mandatory speed governors (40 km/h for school bus, 60/80 km/h for goods/contract carriers) disabled.
vio:SPEED_GOVERNOR_TAMPER.what_to_do_next: Restore speed governor at authorised ASG dealer; obtain seal certificate.
keywords: tampering / disabling speed governor on commercial vehicle

vio:MOD_NO_HEADLIGHT_DRL.name: Two-wheeler AHO (Always Headlight On) disabled post-Apr 2017
keywords: two-wheeler aho (always headlight on) disabled post-apr 2017

vio:MOD_STRUCTURAL.name: Unauthorised structural modification (chassis / engine / colour)
vio:MOD_STRUCTURAL.description: Modifications not approved by RTO; colour change, engine swap, body-kit.
vio:MOD_STRUCTURAL.what_to_do_next: Restore vehicle to factory spec; visit RTO for re-inspection.
vio:MOD_STRUCTURAL.consequence: Fine ₹5,000–10,000; RC may be cancelled (SC judgment 2019).

vio:MOD_ILLEGAL_LED_HID.name: Use of high-intensity / colour-changing lamps
vio:MOD_ILLEGAL_LED_HID.what_to_do_next: Replace with OEM projector. Fine ₹5,000; lamps seized.

vio:MOD_FOG_LAMP_FRONT_ROOF.name: Auxiliary fog lamps on roof / bull-bar
keywords: auxiliary fog lamps on roof / bull-bar

vio:MOD_TINTED_GLASS.name: Tinted glass below permissible VLT
vio:MOD_TINTED_GLASS.description: Front/rear windscreen VLT < 70%, sides VLT < 50% (per Supreme Court 2012).
vio:MOD_TINTED_GLASS.what_to_do_next: Remove tint films. Front/windscreen must allow 70% VLT; sides 50%.

vio:MOD_LASER_JAMMER.name: Installing radar / laser jammer or speed-camera detector
vio:MOD_LASER_JAMMER.description: Vehicles fitted with radar / laser jammers or speed-camera detectors are illegal in India. Vehicle seized.
keywords: installing radar / laser jammer or speed-camera detector

vio:MOD_HSRP_MISSING.name: Missing / non-HSRP high-security registration plate
vio:MOD_HSRP_MISSING.what_to_do_next: Book HSRP online at https://bookmyhsrp.com. Installation fee ₹500–1,500.

vio:DOC_FAKE_DL.name: Using fake / tampered driving licence
vio:DOC_FAKE_DL.what_to_do_next: Non-compoundable criminal offence. Cooperate with officer; legal counsel advised.
vio:DOC_FAKE_DL.officer_action: FIR + vehicle seizure; court attendance mandatory.

vio:DOC_DISOBEY_AUTHORITY.name: Disobeying orders of authorities / refusing information
vio:DOC_DISOBEY_AUTHORITY.description: Refusing to stop or give information to a traffic officer.
vio:DOC_DISOBEY_AUTHORITY.what_to_do_next: Stop when signalled; show documents. Refusing can escalate to a higher offence (Sec 179).
vio:DOC_DISOBEY_AUTHORITY.officer_action: Challan ₹2,000 first time, up to ₹5,000 thereafter.
keywords: disobeying orders of authorities / refusing information

vio:DOC_NO_INSURANCE.name: Driving without vehicle insurance
vio:DOC_NO_INSURANCE.description: Using vehicle without at least third-party insurance cover.
vio:DOC_NO_INSURANCE.what_to_do_next: Park vehicle safely. Buy at least 3rd-party motor insurance online (policy instant). Then drive.
vio:DOC_NO_INSURANCE.tips_to_avoid: Third-party insurance is mandatory since 1988. Renew annually; insurers now sell long-term 3Y/5Y covers for new vehicles.
vio:DOC_NO_INSURANCE.officer_action: Challan; may impound until insurance bought and shown.

vio:DOC_UNAUTHORIZED_USE_VEHICLE.name: Allowing unauthorised / unlicensed driver
vio:DOC_UNAUTHORIZED_USE_VEHICLE.description: Owner allowing a person without a valid DL to drive.

vio:DOC_TAKING_VEHICLE_WITHOUT_AUTH.name: Taking a vehicle without owner's authority
vio:DOC_TAKING_VEHICLE_WITHOUT_AUTH.description: Unauthorised use of someone else's vehicle.
keywords: taking a vehicle without owner's authority

vio:DOC_NO_FITNESS.name: Commercial vehicle without fitness certificate
vio:DOC_NO_FITNESS.description: Transport vehicle plying without fitness certificate.
vio:DOC_NO_FITNESS.what_to_do_next: Do not ply. Book fitness test at authorised Automated Testing Station (ATS). Commercial vehicles >8 yrs require fitness every year.
vio:DOC_NO_FITNESS.tips_to_avoid: Plan fitness well in advance; ATS slots fill fast in metros.

vio:DOC_NO_DL.name: Driving without valid driving licence
vio:DOC_NO_DL.description: Driving a motor vehicle without holding an effective driving licence, or driving a class for which the licence is not endorsed.
vio:DOC_NO_DL.what_to_do_next: Stop the vehicle safely. Do not drive further. Arrange a licensed driver or taxi. Apply for a Learner's Licence at https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in before driving again.
vio:DOC_NO_DL.tips_to_avoid: Always carry a DL digitally on DigiLocker or mParivahan app — accepted as original.
vio:DOC_NO_DL.officer_action: Challan issued; vehicle may be impounded until a licensed driver arrives.
vio:DOC_NO_DL.evidence_req: Photo of the driver behind the wheel + lack of valid DL on Sarathi database.
vio:DOC_NO_DL.common_misconception: A learner's licence alone is NOT sufficient — a licensed adult must be in the front seat and 'L' plates mandatory.

vio:MISC_GENERAL.name: General offence – no specific penalty
vio:MISC_GENERAL.description: Catch-all for violations without specific penalty.

vio:DOC_DISQUALIFIED_DRIVING.name: Driving while disqualified / DL suspended
vio:DOC_DISQUALIFIED_DRIVING.description: Driving despite DL being disqualified or revoked.
vio:DOC_DISQUALIFIED_DRIVING.what_to_do_next: Immediately surrender keys. This is non-compoundable — attend court on summons date.
vio:DOC_DISQUALIFIED_DRIVING.officer_action: Vehicle seized; FIR may be registered.
vio:DOC_DISQUALIFIED_DRIVING.consequence: Imprisonment up to 3 months OR fine up to ₹10,000, or both.

vio:DOC_EXPIRED_RC.name: Driving with expired RC
vio:DOC_EXPIRED_RC.what_to_do_next: Do not drive. Renew within 60 days of expiry via VAHAN 4.0 (Form 25). Late fee ₹300/month.
vio:DOC_EXPIRED_RC.tips_to_avoid: Private vehicle RC valid 15 years; renew before expiry — reminder auto-sent via SMS by RTO.
vio:DOC_EXPIRED_RC.officer_action: Challan; may disallow driving from spot.

vio:DOC_NO_RC.name: Driving without registration certificate (RC)
vio:DOC_NO_RC.description: Using a motor vehicle without valid registration.
vio:DOC_NO_RC.what_to_do_next: Show RC on mParivahan or DigiLocker (digital = valid). If unregistered, stop driving and apply via VAHAN 4.0.
vio:DOC_NO_RC.tips_to_avoid: New vehicles have 30 days from delivery to get permanent registration; do not drive without TR number.
vio:DOC_NO_RC.officer_action: Challan; repeat offence may lead to vehicle seizure.

vio:NOISE_PRESSURE_HORN.name: Use of pressure / multi-toned horn
vio:NOISE_PRESSURE_HORN.what_to_do_next: Replace with factory horn. ₹1,000–2,000 fine; horn seized.
vio:NOISE_PRESSURE_HORN.tips_to_avoid: Pressure / multi-toned / musical horns banned nationally under CMVR 119.

vio:EMIT_POLLUTION_EXCEED.name: Exceeding permissible emission (smoke / CO₂)
vio:EMIT_POLLUTION_EXCEED.what_to_do_next: Get engine tuned; re-test PUC within 7 days.

vio:EMIT_BS_NONCOMPLIANT.name: Non-BS-VI compliant vehicle plying in banned zone
keywords: non-bs-vi compliant vehicle plying in banned zone

vio:NOISE_HORN_SILENT_ZONE.name: Honking in silence zone (hospital / school)
vio:NOISE_HORN_SILENT_ZONE.irc_sign_ref: IRC 67 — Sign No. R-13 'No Horn' (red circle with horn + cross).

vio:DOC_NO_PUC.name: Driving without Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate
vio:DOC_NO_PUC.description: Vehicle plying without valid PUC certificate.
vio:DOC_NO_PUC.what_to_do_next: Visit the nearest PUC centre (list on parivahan.gov.in). Test takes 5 minutes; certificate valid 6 months for BS-IV+, 3 months otherwise.
vio:DOC_NO_PUC.tips_to_avoid: Set a 5-month calendar reminder; keep PUC soft-copy on mParivahan.
vio:DOC_NO_PUC.officer_action: Challan of up to ₹10,000; may disable fuel purchase (Delhi).
keywords: driving without pollution under control (puc) certificate

vio:EMIT_OLD_DIESEL_NCR.name: Diesel vehicle >10 years / petrol >15 years plying in NCR/Delhi
vio:EMIT_OLD_DIESEL_NCR.what_to_do_next: Vehicle cannot ply in NCR. Apply for NOC → re-register in another state (if eligible) or scrap via RVSF.
vio:EMIT_OLD_DIESEL_NCR.tips_to_avoid: Diesel 10-yr / petrol 15-yr age rule applicable in NCR only (NGT 2015 order).
keywords: diesel vehicle >10 years / petrol >15 years plying in ncr/delhi

vio:SIGNAL_DISOBEY_SIGN.name: Disobeying mandatory traffic sign
vio:SIGNAL_DISOBEY_SIGN.description: Ignoring STOP, GIVE WAY, NO HORN, NO ENTRY etc.

vio:SIGNAL_RED_LIGHT_JUMPING.name: Jumping a red traffic light
vio:SIGNAL_RED_LIGHT_JUMPING.description: Crossing a traffic signal when it is red.
vio:SIGNAL_RED_LIGHT_JUMPING.tips_to_avoid: Stop on amber unless already past stop-line; respect all-red phase.
vio:SIGNAL_RED_LIGHT_JUMPING.officer_action: ANPR photo; repeat (>3 in 1 yr) — DL suspension under Sec 183.
vio:SIGNAL_RED_LIGHT_JUMPING.evidence_req: Photo showing red signal + vehicle crossing stop line + timestamp.
vio:SIGNAL_RED_LIGHT_JUMPING.licence_action: Licence may be suspended on repeat (s.19)

vio:SIGNAL_DISOBEY_POLICE_SIGNAL.name: Disobeying a traffic police signal
vio:SIGNAL_DISOBEY_POLICE_SIGNAL.description: Ignoring hand signals / whistle from police.
vio:SIGNAL_DISOBEY_POLICE_SIGNAL.what_to_do_next: Apologise, cooperate. Fine ₹2,000 first time, up to ₹5,000.
vio:SIGNAL_DISOBEY_POLICE_SIGNAL.evidence_req: Body-cam or dash-cam footage if available.

vio:DANGER_RACING.name: Racing / speed-trial on public road
vio:DANGER_RACING.what_to_do_next: Stop racing. Non-compoundable. ₹5,000 fine; 3-month imprisonment possible.
vio:DANGER_RACING.licence_action: Licence may be impounded and suspended (s.206(4))

vio:DANGER_STUNT_WHEELIE.name: Stunt riding / wheelie / drifting on public road
keywords: stunt riding / wheelie / drifting on public road

vio:DANGER_UNSAFE_VEHICLE.name: Driving a vehicle in unsafe condition
keywords: driving a vehicle in unsafe condition

vio:DANGER_RASH_DRIVING.name: Rash / negligent driving
vio:DANGER_RASH_DRIVING.description: Driving in a manner dangerous to public.
vio:DANGER_RASH_DRIVING.officer_action: If causing injury — BNS Sec 125/106 may apply.
vio:DANGER_RASH_DRIVING.licence_action: Licence may be impounded and suspended (s.206(4))

vio:CRIM_HURT_RASH_NEGLIGENT.name: Causing hurt by rash or negligent driving
vio:CRIM_HURT_RASH_NEGLIGENT.description: Rash or negligent driving that injures another person. Hurt and grievous hurt carry different terms.
vio:CRIM_HURT_RASH_NEGLIGENT.what_to_do_next: Get the injured person medical help, report to police within 24 hours (MV Act s.134), and consult a lawyer; this is a criminal case decided by a court.
vio:CRIM_HURT_RASH_NEGLIGENT.tips_to_avoid: Drive within limits and keep a safe distance, especially near two-wheelers and pedestrians.
vio:CRIM_HURT_RASH_NEGLIGENT.officer_action: FIR registered; vehicle may be seized for inspection.
vio:CRIM_HURT_RASH_NEGLIGENT.evidence_req: Medical report, scene photos, witness statements.

vio:CRIM_RASH_DRIVING_PUBLIC_WAY.name: Rash driving on a public way (criminal)
vio:CRIM_RASH_DRIVING_PUBLIC_WAY.description: Driving so rashly or negligently that human life is endangered; charged alongside MV Act s.184 when people were put at risk.
vio:CRIM_RASH_DRIVING_PUBLIC_WAY.what_to_do_next: This is a criminal charge decided by a court; keep the challan/FIR copy and consult a lawyer.
vio:CRIM_RASH_DRIVING_PUBLIC_WAY.tips_to_avoid: No racing, stunts or weaving through traffic on public roads.
vio:CRIM_RASH_DRIVING_PUBLIC_WAY.officer_action: FIR may be registered in addition to the MV Act challan.
vio:CRIM_RASH_DRIVING_PUBLIC_WAY.evidence_req: Video, witness statements, damage or injury evidence.

vio:LIGHT_NO_HEADLIGHTS_NIGHT.name: Driving at night without headlights
vio:LIGHT_NO_HEADLIGHTS_NIGHT.description: Driving after dark without headlamps or tail lamps switched on or working.
vio:LIGHT_NO_HEADLIGHTS_NIGHT.what_to_do_next: Pay the challan and fix or switch on the lamps before driving again.
vio:LIGHT_NO_HEADLIGHTS_NIGHT.tips_to_avoid: Check headlamps and tail lamps before night trips; two-wheelers from 2017 keep headlights always on.

vio:SAFETY_FOOTBOARD_TRAVEL.name: Passengers travelling on the footboard
vio:SAFETY_FOOTBOARD_TRAVEL.description: Allowing passengers to stand or hang on the footboard or steps of a bus.
vio:SAFETY_FOOTBOARD_TRAVEL.what_to_do_next: Pay the challan; passengers must be moved inside before the bus continues.
vio:SAFETY_FOOTBOARD_TRAVEL.tips_to_avoid: Close doors before moving; do not start while anyone is on the steps.
vio:SAFETY_FOOTBOARD_TRAVEL.officer_action: Challan to the conductor and driver.

MV Act 1988 §134.title: Duty of driver in case of accident and injury
MV Act 1988 §134.summary: Driver must secure medical attention for the injured and report the accident to police within 24 hours.
MV Act 1988 §134.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §161.title: Compensation in hit-and-run cases
MV Act 1988 §161.summary: Victims of hit-and-run get fixed compensation from the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund: ₹2,00,000 for death, ₹50,000 for grievous hurt. Claim through the district claims enquiry officer.
MV Act 1988 §161.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §177.title: General penalty
MV Act 1988 §177.summary: Contravention with no specific penalty: fine up to ₹500; repeat up to ₹1,500.
MV Act 1988 §177.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §180.title: Allowing unauthorised persons to drive
MV Act 1988 §180.summary: Owner or person in charge who lets someone without a valid licence drive: up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
MV Act 1988 §180.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §181.title: Driving without licence / underage
MV Act 1988 §181.summary: Driving without a licence or below the minimum age: up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
MV Act 1988 §181.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §184.title: Driving dangerously
MV Act 1988 §184.summary: First offence: 6 months to 1 year, or fine ₹1,000–5,000, or both. Repeat within 3 years: up to 2 years, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
MV Act 1988 §184.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §185.title: Driving by a drunken person or under drugs
MV Act 1988 §185.summary: First offence: up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both. Repeat within 3 years: up to 2 years, or fine up to ₹15,000, or both.
MV Act 1988 §185.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §187.title: Offences relating to accident
MV Act 1988 §187.summary: Failing to stop, help or report under s.132/133/134: up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.
MV Act 1988 §187.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §194.title: Driving vehicle exceeding permissible weight
MV Act 1988 §194.summary: Whoever drives or causes or allows an overloaded goods vehicle: ₹20,000 plus ₹2,000 per extra tonne; the excess load must be offloaded.
MV Act 1988 §194.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §194A.title: Carriage of excess passengers
MV Act 1988 §194A.summary: Whoever drives or causes or allows a transport vehicle to carry excess passengers: ₹200 per extra passenger.
MV Act 1988 §194A.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §194B.title: Safety belts and child restraints
MV Act 1988 §194B.summary: Driving without a seat belt or carrying passengers not wearing seat belts: ₹1,000. Child under 14 not secured: ₹1,000.
MV Act 1988 §194B.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §194C.title: Overloading of two-wheelers
MV Act 1988 §194C.summary: More than one pillion: ₹1,000 and licence disqualification for 3 months.
MV Act 1988 §194C.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §194D.title: Protective headgear
MV Act 1988 §194D.summary: Rider or pillion without a helmet: ₹1,000 and licence disqualification for 3 months.
MV Act 1988 §194D.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §196.title: Driving uninsured vehicle
MV Act 1988 §196.summary: Whoever drives or causes or allows an uninsured vehicle: up to 3 months, or ₹2,000, or both; repeat ₹4,000.
MV Act 1988 §196.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

MV Act 1988 §199A.title: Offences by juveniles
MV Act 1988 §199A.summary: When a juvenile commits an offence, the guardian or owner is deemed guilty: up to 3 years and ₹25,000. Registration cancelled for 12 months; the juvenile cannot get a licence until 25. The juvenile is dealt with under the Juvenile Justice Act.
MV Act 1988 §199A.source_title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended by the MV (Amendment) Act, 2019)

BNS 2023 §106(1).title: Causing death by negligence
BNS 2023 §106(1).summary: Causing death by a rash or negligent act: up to 5 years and fine.

BNS 2023 §106(2).title: Death by rash driving and escaping
BNS 2023 §106(2).summary: Causing death by rash or negligent driving and escaping without reporting: up to 10 years and fine. Not yet in force (kept in abeyance).
BNS 2023 §106(2).note: Not notified as of the 1 July 2024 commencement.

BNS 2023 §125.title: Act endangering life or personal safety
BNS 2023 §125.summary: Rash or negligent act endangering life: up to 3 months or ₹2,500. Causing hurt: up to 6 months or ₹5,000. Causing grievous hurt: up to 3 years or ₹10,000.

BNS 2023 §281.title: Rash driving on a public way
BNS 2023 §281.summary: Driving so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life: up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
